The Weird Guy - MIJ19 - Amaterasu Selvedge is made in Japan from 11.5oz Japanese selvedge denim with a natural indigo rope-dyed warp and a beige weft. The Weird Guy fit has a mid rise and a tapered leg.
The MIJ19 Amaterasu Selvedge takes its name from Amaterasu, the sun goddess of Shinto mythology and the mythical ancestor of the Japanese Imperial Family. Her name, 天照 (Amaterasu), reflects both her identity and her role. Ama (天) means “heaven,” while terasu (照) means “to shine” or “to illuminate.” Together, they describe her divine duty to illuminate the heavens and bring light to the world. Amaterasu is revered as the highest-ranking kami in the Shinto pantheon, standing above the countless deities often referred to as the “eight million gods.”
Just as Amaterasu’s light illuminates the heavens, this fabric is defined by brightness and warmth. Woven in Japan from 11.5oz selvedge denim, the warp yarns are rope dyed with natural indigo, creating a soft, luminous shade of blue. The rope-dyeing process leaves the core of each warp yarn white, allowing the denim to develop a classic range of blue-to-white fades with wear.

p-nakedandfamousdenim-14984427176301.d:
The FoxFibre® Green Weft Selvedge is a 13oz Japanese selvedge denim that pairs indigo rope-dyed warp yarns with a naturally colored FoxFibre® weft. The distinctive green-grey tone comes from natural green FoxFibre® cotton that has been treated with iron, a traditional mineral-based process used to deepen and stabilize naturally occurring color. Rather than adding dye, the iron reacts with the cotton’s inherent pigment, resulting in an earthy green-grey tone that becomes more pronounced with washing and wear.
FoxFibre® was developed by cotton breeder and environmental pioneer Sally Fox, who began her work in the 1980s by selectively breeding naturally pigmented cotton varieties to eliminate the need for conventional dyeing. Because the color is grown into the fiber itself, FoxFibre® significantly reduces the environmental impact associated with chemical dyes and finishing.

Our traditional straight cut jeans, made from 19oz left-hand twill selvedge denim. While most of our denims feature a traditional right-hand twill weave — characterised by a diagonal grain running from the top-right to the bottom-left of the fabric — this “lefty” denim is woven in the opposite direction under very high tension. This creates one of our stiffest, most robust fabrics, with an intense indigo hue that tends to fade with higher contrast than looser weaves.
To create this darkened variation, we take a pair of standard IH-634S-19L jeans and steep the entire garment in black dye using a direct dyeing process. This stains the indigo denim and stitching, with the added bonus of removing all shrinkage from the fabric. A unique middle ground between our traditional indigo and black denims, over time the fabric will gradually fade with blue-tinged hues in high-wear areas.

The original US Army M-1943 is often considered to be the godfather of the modern military “Field Jacket” — setting a blueprint for all that followed and serving as a predecessor to the iconic M-65. Its design significantly improved upon the inadequate M-41 from a few years earlier, offering a wider array of pockets, fuller body coverage, and a roomier fit that could be layered with a wool liner for warmth during WWII and later the Korean War.
New for FW26, Iron Heart’s take on the M-43 honours its heritage while updating the design with a few typical over-engineered upgrades. Made from vintage-style 9.5oz back sateen fabric — pigment-dyed to allow for gradual, low-contrast fading over time — we’ve fitted the jacket with a Japanese Ventile lining for an added layer of water resistance, oversized four-hole buttons to ensure secure fastenings, and poly/cotton stitching throughout for strength. The result is a versatile, functional and highly durable outer layer that doesn’t compromise its authentic 1940s military styling.
